gap_map.why_it_matters: Router scaffolding produces endpoints fast. Nothing decides which of them carry business rules worth testing, so the suite ends up asserting that FastAPI can serialize a model.
gap_map.filled_by: LambdaTest/agent-skills#pytest-skill for authoring, trailofbits/skills#property-based-testing for invariants

gap_map.why_it_matters: The listed skills stop at the request/response boundary. Schema changes are the single most common source of irreversible production damage in this stack.
gap_map.fallback: The mentor requires every schema change to ship with a reversible migration and a plan for the deploy window.

layers.name: unit
layers.belongs_here: pure business rules and validation logic
layers.signal_you_picked_wrong: the test constructs a Request object just to call a rule

layers.name: integration
layers.belongs_here: the real app through TestClient, with dependency overrides for what leaves the process
layers.cost: moderate - and this is where the real defects are

layers.name: contract
layers.belongs_here: that the response shape matches what clients depend on

testing.proportions: FastAPI team: test through TestClient with normal def functions, not async def, so pytest runs without complications. They recommend exercising the real request/response cycle rather than mocking the app.
rules: Test through TestClient against the real app. It exercises dependency resolution, validation and serialization - where the defects actually are.
Test functions are normal def, not async def. The team states this explicitly.
Replace external systems with dependency_overrides, not by monkeypatching module internals. The override is the supported seam.
Every endpoint has at least one test for its failure response, not only its success response.
Clear dependency_overrides between tests or one test's override silently configures the next.
traps: Mocking the router instead of using TestClient skips validation and serialization - the layers most likely to be wrong.
A leaked dependency_overrides entry makes a later test pass for the wrong reason.
async def test functions without the right plugin either never run or run outside the app's event loop.
A response_model silently drops fields, so the test asserts the trimmed output while the endpoint returns more than declared.
Module-level state and mutable defaults survive between tests in the same process.
what_not_to_test: That Pydantic validates types, or that FastAPI parses a path parameter.
Generated OpenAPI output, unless it is a published contract.
Alembic migration files as units - exercise them by running them.
testing.notes: Prefer FastAPI's TestClient for integration tests over mocking the router - it exercises dependency overrides, validation and serialization, which is where the real bugs are. Read pyproject.toml for the configured runner and typechecker before assuming these commands.

growth_thresholds.extract_service_layer: an endpoint function exceeds 40 lines, which means business logic has leaked into the transport layer
growth_thresholds.extract_package: >=2 features import the same internal module

layers.name: Router
layers.must_not: hold business rules - an endpoint past 40 lines has absorbed the service

layers.name: Service
layers.must_not: import fastapi - a module that raises HTTPException is not a service

layers.name: Schemas
layers.holds: Pydantic models for the transport contract
layers.must_not: double as ORM models - one changes for the API, the other for the database

variants.name: Routers only
variants.use_when: a small service with few rules
variants.cost: rules end up in endpoints and become unreachable from a worker or a CLI

variants.name: Routers plus a service layer
variants.use_when: the same rules serve HTTP and anything else
variants.cost: one more hop, unnecessary while HTTP is the only caller

rules: A path operation does transport only: validate, delegate, shape the response.
A service module never imports fastapi. Raising HTTPException from a service ties business rules to the web layer.
Transport schemas and database models are separate types even when identical - they change for different reasons.
Dependencies are the injection seam. Anything the tests need to replace is a dependency, not a module-level import.
architecture.notes: FastAPI documents a bigger-applications router layout but does not prescribe a service layer. The service-layer rules here are the mentor's judgment, not the maintainers' - present them as such.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: FastAPI supports both, and mixing them badly blocks the event loop with no visible error.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Pick one for data access and stay with it.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: A blocking call inside an async path operation stalls every concurrent request - it looks like a performance problem, not a bug.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: No ORM is bundled, and where a session opens and closes is not decided for you.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Session per request, provided as a dependency.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: A session shared across requests leaks data between users; one never closed exhausts the pool under load.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: Pydantic schemas and ORM models look interchangeable and are not.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Separate. They change for different reasons.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Shared types turn a database column rename into an unintended API breaking change.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: FastAPI ships security utilities but no policy.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Decide where the check lives - dependency, middleware or gateway - and keep it in one place.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Authorization enforced in two places is authorization forgotten in one.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: BackgroundTasks, a worker queue and a scheduler have very different delivery guarantees.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: BackgroundTasks only for work that may be lost.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: BackgroundTasks vanish when the process restarts - work you assumed was queued was never durable.

operability.observability: Structured logging plus an exception handler registered on the app. Without a handler an unhandled error becomes a 500 with nothing recorded.
operability.authorization: A dependency on the path operation, or middleware. An endpoint with no security dependency is public - and looks identical to one that is public on purpose.
done_checks: the app boots with the real configuration
clean install from a fresh clone
rules: Every path operation states its authorization decision explicitly.
Every outbound call has a timeout. httpx without one waits forever and takes a worker with it.
Database sessions are per request and always closed, including on the error path.
Configuration is validated at boot, not read ad hoc with os.environ.get scattered through modules.
Schema changes ship with a reversible migration and a plan for the deploy window.

dead_code_risks: Endpoints registered by decorator and reachable only over HTTP
Pydantic models referenced only as type annotations in signatures
Alembic migration modules discovered by directory scan
Dependencies wired through Depends() with a callable reference
Celery or background tasks dispatched by string name
Plugins loaded through entry points declared in pyproject.toml
